VERDICT: DISAGREE, on one reproduced defect. FINDING 1 (correctness, reproduced, blocking): lwb_proof_coverage reports a FALSE POSITIVE for any landed deliverable whose proof record is named after its BRANCH rather than its PR number -- a naming style this repository not only permits but uses, in this very PR (proof/lwb-ship-proof-coverage-integrity.json, which declares "pr": 49). adapters/claude/repo_facts.collect_landed_unproven builds 'known' from collect_proof_ids_ex, which returns record FILENAME STEMS only, and then tests 'pr not in known' with pr as the digit string scraped from the squash subject. A record that identifies its PR in its CONTENT, not its filename, is therefore invisible to the match. CI's scripts/lwb_check_proof.py::check_coverage does not have this defect: it reads each record's JSON and adds data['pr'] to proved_prs (lines 536-558), then skips the commit. REPRODUCTION, run on this head: scratch git repo with proof/my-feature.json containing {"pr": 77, ...} and a loose commit whose subject is 'Some landed thing (#77)'. CI's record scan -> proved_prs={77}, 77 in proved_prs -> CI SKIPS the commit. The hook adapter -> collect_proof_ids == ['my-feature'], collect_landed_unproven == ('7fb313b7ba62 (#77)',) -> the rule FIRES, telling the user a proven deliverable has no proof record and to 'Add a proof/<id>.json for each' -- which they already did. Why this is blocking rather than a note: the module docstring of core/lwb_core/rules/lwb_proof_coverage.py and collect_landed_unproven's own docstring both make an explicit, falsifiable claim about exactly this axis -- 'This under-matches on purpose ... a merge this scan cannot see is a missed warning, not a FALSE one' -- and docs/rules/lwb-proof-coverage.md says 'Same shape of check as CI's check_coverage'. The over-match above falsifies all three. The limitation is disclosed nowhere in the module, the doc, or the PR body's 'Not tested / could not verify' list, and the test suite does not cover it: tests/adapters/test_claude_repo_facts_landed_unproven.py's only positive-match case (test_a_squash_merge_subject_with_a_matching_record_is_silent) writes proof/41.json, i.e. the PR-number-named style exclusively. Blast radius is bounded -- the rule ships at "warn", so this is a spurious warning, not a denied action -- but a newly shipped gate that misreports a compliant repo, while its own docstring asserts it cannot, is the shape this repo spends its review budget on. Fix is small and has precedent inside this same PR: collect_matched_proof_facts already reads one record's content under a size bound, so reading the 'pr' field of candidate records (or, at minimum, amending the two docstrings, the doc and the finding text to name this class of false positive) is available without breaking the no-subprocess boundary. FINDING 2 (secondary, non-blocking, recorded not charged): collect_matched_proof_facts collapses 'could not check' into 'checked, clean' inside a record it DID read, on two fields that are typed Optional[bool] and so have a None channel available for exactly that distinction. A record missing 'checked_by', or carrying a non-string one, yields self_certified=False (not None); a commands[] entry whose 'exit'/'expect_exit' are absent or non-integer is skipped, so a record CI's _validate_record would reject as malformed (lines 147-172) reads as has_failed_command=False. Both are under-reports in warn mode, so neither produces a false accusation, and the docs correctly describe None as no-opinion at the whole-record level; I record this because 'I could not check' sharing a representation with 'I checked and found nothing' is this repo's named defect pattern (HANDOFF.md item 5) and here it is reintroduced one level down, inside a record that was read.
